note: Crucible adversarial review completed with 5 key findings spanning process management, authentication state machine, logging race conditions, deployment scripting, and data migration.

findings.message: When the supervisor restarts, all open pipe handles (including the stdin pipe redirected to the job) are closed by the OS. The running job's stdin will receive an EOF immediately. It is impossible for the restarted supervisor to write to the stdin of a re-adopted job, meaning any pending or future AskUserQuestion prompt for that job will fail.

Rotating the ANCHOR_TOKEN will break the installed iPhone PWA because its start URL is fixed at installation time on iOS. A PWA launch after rotation will present the old token, failing authentication with no way for the phone to automatically update its start URL, forcing a manual deletion and re-adding of the PWA.

Running the reconciler 'on demand' on a live service can cause race conditions. An active, in-flight mutation that has appended an INTENT but not yet completed its legacy write or CONFIRM could be falsely aborted or confirmed by the reconciler. The reconciler must either run only when the engine is quiescent (e.g. strict startup boot phase) or exclude intents younger than a safety tail window.

The script install_supervisor.ps1 attempts to set the NSSM service ObjectName to a custom user account (.\john) without prompting for or storing a password. On Windows, service configuration for custom user accounts requires a password; without it, the service will fail to install or fail to start with a logon error.

The Step-A rollback plan claims 'no data reconstruction, because the original dir was never mutated.' However, if the rollback is executed after the migrated service has run and accepted new user mutations, reverting to the original directory will cause data loss of all mutations made post-migration.
